toolkit.name: OneDrive
toolkit.description: OneDrive is Microsoft’s cloud storage solution enabling users to store, sync, and share files across devices, offering offline access, real-time collaboration, and enterprise-grade security

tools.name: Check In Drive Item
tools.description: Tool to check in a checked out driveItem resource, making the version of the document available to others. Use when you need to check in a file that was previously checked out in OneDrive or SharePoint.

comment.title: Comment
comment.description: A check-in comment that is associated with the version.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the item to check in.

check_in_as.title: Check In As
check_in_as.description: Optional. The status of the document after the check-in operation is complete. Can be 'published' or unspecified.

drive_item_id.title: Drive Item Id
drive_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the driveItem to check in.

tools.name: Checkout Drive Item
tools.description: Tool to check out a driveItem to prevent others from editing it and make your changes invisible until checked in. Use when you need to lock a file for exclusive editing in SharePoint or OneDrive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the item to checkout.

drive_item_id.title: Drive Item Id
drive_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the driveItem (file or folder) to checkout.

tools.name: Close Workbook Session
tools.description: Close an Excel workbook session without deleting the workbook.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: DriveItem ID of the workbook whose session is being closed.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: Drive containing the workbook. Use 'me' for the connected user's drive, or provide a Microsoft Graph drive ID.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Workbook session ID returned by ONE_DRIVE_CREATE_WORKBOOK_SESSION.

tools.name: Copy Item
tools.description: Tool to copy a DriveItem (file or folder) to a new location asynchronously. Use when you need to duplicate an item, optionally renaming it or specifying a different parent folder. The operation is asynchronous; the response provides a URL to monitor the copy progress. Do not assume the copy is complete immediately; verify via ONE_DRIVE_GET_ITEM or by listing the destination, especially for large folder trees.

name.title: Name
name.description: The new name for the copied item. If not provided, the same name as the original is used. Recommended to provide either 'name' or 'parent_reference' for reliable operation.
name.human_parameter_description: The name you want for the copied item. If not provided, keeps the original name. Recommended to specify a new name or destination folder.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The ID of the DriveItem to be copied.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the file or folder you want to copy. You can get this from a previous item list or search.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The ID of the site if the item is in a SharePoint site.
site_id.human_parameter_description: If the item is in a SharePoint site, enter that site’s ID so we can find the item there.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The ID of the user if accessing another user's drive.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Use this when copying from another person’s OneDrive. Enter their user ID or email; leave blank to use your own.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The ID of the drive where the item is located. If not provided, 'me' (user's default drive) is assumed.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The specific drive that contains the item to copy. Leave blank to use your own drive.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The ID of the group if the item is in a group drive.
group_id.human_parameter_description: If the item lives in a Microsoft 365 group drive, enter that group's ID so we know where to look.

children_only.title: Children Only
children_only.description: If set to true, only the children of the source driveItem (if it's a folder) are copied, not the driveItem itself. Defaults to false. Cannot be used with name parameter.
children_only.human_parameter_description: Copy only the contents of a folder, not the folder itself. Turn this on when you want to merge the contents into an existing destination folder.

parent_reference.title: CopyItemParentReference

id.title: Id
id.description: The ID of the parent item.

driveId.title: Drive Id
driveId.description: The ID of the drive that contains the parent item.

parent_reference.description: Reference to the parent item (folder) where the copy will be created. If not provided, the item is copied to the same location. Recommended to provide either 'name' or 'parent_reference' for reliable operation. Must use stable OneDrive item IDs (not paths or names), as paths break on rename/relocation. Resolve names/paths first using ONE_DRIVE_SEARCH_ITEMS or ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_FIND_FOLDER. Expected keys: `driveId` and `id`.
parent_reference.human_parameter_description: Where you want the copy to be created. If not provided, copies to the same location as the original. Recommended to specify a new name or destination folder.

conflict_behavior.title: @Microsoft.Graph.Conflict Behavior
conflict_behavior.description: Specifies how to handle a naming conflict if an item with the same name already exists in the destination. 'fail' (default), 'replace', or 'rename'.
conflict_behavior.human_parameter_description: What to do if an item with the same name already exists at the destination: fail, replace, or rename. Pick this to avoid accidental overwrites.

include_all_version_history.title: Include All Version History
include_all_version_history.description: If set to true, the version history of the source file is copied to the destination. Defaults to false.
include_all_version_history.human_parameter_description: Include the file’s version history in the copy. Enable this if you need previous versions preserved.

tools.name: Create Drive Item Permission
tools.description: Tool to create a new permission on a OneDrive drive item. Use when you need to grant application or SharePoint group permissions to a file or folder. This endpoint supports creating application permissions and SharePoint site group permissions only.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Array of Microsoft Graph role strings to assign to the permission. Documented/common values include read, write, and owner for SharePoint/OneDrive for Business permission resources; tenant/resource-specific roles may also be accepted by Graph.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive.

drive_item_id.title: Drive Item Id
drive_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item.

granted_to_v2.title: Granted To V2

siteGroup.title: SiteGroupIdentity

id.title: Id
id.description: The unique identifier of the SharePoint site group.

displayName.title: Display Name
displayName.description: The display name of the SharePoint site group.

siteGroup.description: Represents a SharePoint site group identity.

id.title: Id
id.description: The unique identifier of the application.

displayName.title: Display Name
displayName.description: The display name of the application.

granted_to_v2.description: The identity to grant permission to. Must contain either application or siteGroup property.

tools.name: Create Sharing Link
tools.description: Tool to create a sharing link for a DriveItem (file or folder) by its unique ID. Use when you need to generate a shareable link for an item in OneDrive or SharePoint.

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of sharing link to create. Valid values: `view`, `edit`, `embed`.
type.human_parameter_description: Choose the kind of link to create—view-only, edit, or embed—based on how you want others to interact with the item.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: The scope of the sharing link. `anonymous`: anyone with the link can use it; choose it only when the user explicitly asks for anonymous or 'anyone with the link' access, never by inference. `organization`: people signed in to the tenant; available only in OneDrive for Business and SharePoint. `users`: only the people listed in `recipients`; requires a non-empty `recipients` list, and is assumed automatically when recipients are provided with no scope. Embed and password-protected links are OneDrive Personal only and support neither `organization` nor `users`. Prefer choosing a scope explicitly: if omitted with no recipients, Microsoft Graph applies the tenant's default sharing-link scope, which may be `anonymous`. Tenant policy may also block a scope or downgrade the created link to a more restrictive one than requested, so check the scope on the returned link.
scope.human_parameter_description: Who can use the link: anyone with the link (anonymous), people in your organization, or specific people you list as recipients. Pick one explicitly; if left empty with no recipients, your organization's default sharing setting applies and may allow anyone with the link.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item (file or folder) for which to create the link. Note: Some item types cannot be shared, including embedded objects, certain system files, and items with restricted permissions. If sharing fails with 'notSupported' error, verify the item type supports sharing.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the file or folder you want to share. You can get it from the item's link or from a previous search or list operation. Note: Some items (like embedded objects or system files) cannot be shared.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the site. Use this if the item is in a SharePoint site's drive.
site_id.human_parameter_description: Use this for items stored in a SharePoint site. Provide the site’s ID to create the link from that site’s drive.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user. Use this if the item is in another user's drive.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Enter the ID or email address of the user whose OneDrive contains the item. Leave empty to use your own drive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. If not provided, the link will be created in the current user's drive (me/drive).
drive_id.human_parameter_description: Specify the drive that contains the item if it isn’t your own. Use this when sharing from a specific OneDrive or SharePoint drive.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of the group. Use this if the item is in a group's drive.
group_id.human_parameter_description: Use this if the item lives in a Microsoft 365 group’s drive. Enter the group’s ID to target that drive.

password.title: Password
password.description: The password for the sharing link. Optional and OneDrive Personal only.
password.human_parameter_description: Optional password people must enter to open the link. Helpful when sharing sensitive files.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.description: The people to share with when scope is 'users'. Required when scope is 'users'; if provided while scope is omitted, scope defaults to 'users'; not allowed with scope 'anonymous' or 'organization' (an empty list is treated as omitted). Each recipient is an object with one of `email`, `alias`, or `objectId`, e.g. [{'email': 'user@example.com'}]; recipient contents are validated by Microsoft Graph, not by this action.
recipients.human_parameter_description: The people you want to share with when using scope 'users'. For each person, provide an email address, Microsoft account alias, or Microsoft Entra object ID.

expiration_date_time.title: Expiration Date Time
expiration_date_time.description: The expiration date and time for the permission, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. Example: 2023-12-31T23:59:59Z Must be a future UTC timestamp; past values will cause the call to fail.
expiration_date_time.human_parameter_description: When the link should stop working. Provide a UTC date and time to automatically turn off access.

retain_inherited_permissions.title: Retain Inherited Permissions
retain_inherited_permissions.description: If true (default), existing inherited permissions are retained. If false, all existing permissions are removed when sharing for the first time.
retain_inherited_permissions.human_parameter_description: Keep existing permissions when you share (recommended). Turn off only if you want to remove prior access and start fresh.

tools.name: Create SharePoint List Item
tools.description: Create an item in a SharePoint list using Microsoft Graph through the OneDrive connection. Use when you need to add a new row/item to a SharePoint list after resolving the site ID and list ID.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Field values for the new list item, keyed by SharePoint internal column name. For a basic custom list, include at least {'Title': 'New item'}.
fields.human_parameter_description: The column values to save on the new list item. Use SharePoint internal column names such as Title.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The unique Microsoft Graph ID of the SharePoint list where the item will be created. Use ONE_DRIVE_LIST_SITE_LISTS to find list IDs.
list_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the SharePoint list where the item should be created.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The Microsoft Graph SharePoint site ID in composite format, usually 'hostname,site-collection-id,web-id'. Use ONE_DRIVE_GET_SITE_DETAILS or ONE_DRIVE_LIST_SITE_LISTS outputs to confirm the site ID.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The SharePoint site ID that contains the list. It usually looks like hostname,GUID,GUID.

tools.name: Create Workbook Session
tools.description: Create a persistent or temporary session for an Excel workbook.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: DriveItem ID of the Office Open XML workbook.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: Drive containing the workbook. Use 'me' for the connected user's drive, or provide a Microsoft Graph drive ID.

persist_changes.title: Persist Changes
persist_changes.description: True to save workbook changes; false to create a temporary, non-persistent session copy.

tools.name: Delete Item
tools.description: Tool to delete a DriveItem (file or folder) by its unique ID from the authenticated user's OneDrive. Use when you need to remove an item from OneDrive. This action moves the item to the recycle bin, not permanently deleting it; storage quota is not freed until the recycle bin is emptied. Bulk deletions can trigger 429 (rate limit) or 5xx responses — limit concurrency and use exponential backoff.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the DriveItem (file or folder) to be deleted.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the file or folder you want to delete from OneDrive. You can get this from a previous list/search or from the item's link or details page.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's ID, email, or 'me'. Defaults to 'me' (authenticated user). Required for S2S (app-only) auth.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the Drive where the item is located. If not provided, the action will target the user's personal OneDrive (me/drive). Always specify drive_id explicitly for group drives, SharePoint site drives, or shared libraries to avoid silently querying the wrong drive.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The OneDrive or SharePoint drive where the item is stored. Leave this blank to use your own OneDrive.

if_match.title: If Match
if_match.description: (Optional) If this request header is included and the eTag (or cTag) provided doesn't match the current tag on the item, a `412 Precondition Failed` response is returned, and the item won't be deleted.
if_match.human_parameter_description: Optional: include the item's version tag to delete it only if it hasn't changed since you last saw it. This helps prevent deleting an item that was updated by someone else.

tools.name: Permanently Delete Drive Item
tools.description: Tool to permanently delete a driveItem by its ID without moving it to the recycle bin. Use when you need to irreversibly remove a file or folder from OneDrive or SharePoint. This action cannot be undone.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item (file or folder) to permanently delete. This action deletes the item without moving it to the recycle bin and cannot be undone.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the item to permanently delete.

tools.name: Delete Drive Item Permission
tools.description: Tool to delete a permission from a drive item. Use when you need to revoke sharing access to a file or folder. Only non-inherited sharing permissions can be deleted.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item (file or folder).

perm_id.title: Perm Id
perm_id.description: The unique identifier of the permission to delete. Only non-inherited sharing permissions can be deleted.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of a SharePoint site. Use this if the item is in a SharePoint site's drive.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of a user. Use this if the item is in a specific user's drive (other than 'me').

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. If not provided, the action will target the user's personal OneDrive (me/drive).

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of the group. Use this if the item is in a group's drive.

tools.name: Delete Shares Permission
tools.description: Tool to delete the permission navigation property for a shared drive item. Use when you need to remove a sharing link permission. This effectively revokes access via the specific share link.

shared_drive_item_id.title: Shared Drive Item Id
shared_drive_item_id.description: The share ID or base64-encoded sharing URL. This is the shareId returned from the createLink API response. Example format: u!aHR0cHM6Ly9jb21wb3NpbzIwMjQtbXkuc2hhcmVwb2ludC5jb20vOng6L2cvcGVyc29uYWwva2FyYW52YWlkeWFfYXV0aGtpdF9haS9JUURPT2NCVEx5RTFSWktVQkJGZ0YzZVZBUmI4Zk5XVjdhMUJidGQ1NDF2SEdXUQ

tools.name: Delete SharePoint Item Permission
tools.description: Revoke a Microsoft Graph beta permission from a SharePoint list or list item.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: Optional SharePoint list item ID. Provide this to revoke a list-item permission; omit it to revoke a list-level permission.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The list item ID when revoking a list-item permission. Leave empty for list-level permissions.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The unique Microsoft Graph ID of the SharePoint list.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The Microsoft Graph SharePoint site ID in composite format, usually 'hostname,site-collection-id,web-id'.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The SharePoint site ID containing the list or list item.

permission_id.title: Permission Id
permission_id.description: The Microsoft Graph permission ID to revoke.
permission_id.human_parameter_description: The permission ID returned by the corresponding permission listing endpoint.

tools.name: Discard Checkout
tools.description: Tool to discard the checkout of a driveItem, releasing it and discarding any changes made while checked out. Use when you need to cancel a checkout and revert changes on a file in SharePoint or OneDrive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the item to discard checkout.

drive_item_id.title: Drive Item Id
drive_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the driveItem (file or folder) to discard checkout.

tools.name: Download a file
tools.description: Downloads a file from a user's OneDrive using its item ID, which must refer to a file and not a folder. Response contains a content object with the downloaded file, MIME type, and name; raw file data is not returned directly. Parsing content from Excel, Word, PDF, or other formats requires additional tooling. The downloaded file can be passed to downstream tools such as OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL or OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT.

format.title: Format
format.description: Optional format for file conversion during download. 'pdf' converts supported source files (doc, docx, dot, dotx, dotm, dsn, dwg, eml, epub, fluidframework, form, htm, html, loop, loot, markdown, md, msg, note, odp, ods, odt, page, pps, ppsx, ppt, pptx, pulse, rtf, task, tif, tiff, wbtx, whiteboard, xls, xlsm, xlsx) to PDF. 'html' converts Loop/Fluid files (loop, fluid, wbtx) to HTML. Leave empty to download the file in its original format without conversion. Do NOT use this parameter if the file is already in the target format (e.g., don't convert PDF to PDF or HTML to HTML), as this will result in an error.
format.human_parameter_description: Choose a format to convert the file during download. Select 'pdf' to convert supported documents to PDF, or 'html' to convert Loop/Fluid files to HTML. Leave empty to download the original file. Important: Only use this when converting FROM one format TO another (e.g., DOCX to PDF). Do not attempt to convert a file to the same format it's already in (e.g., PDF to PDF).

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: Raw item ID only (e.g., '1234567890ABC'). Do not include URL fragments or query parameters like '&cid=...' or '?param=...' from sharing links.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the specific file you want to download. Provide only the raw item ID, not a full URL or URL fragment with query parameters.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's ID or User Principal Name (UPN), or 'me' for the authenticated user's OneDrive. Ignored when drive_id is provided.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose OneDrive you want to access to download a file. Use 'me' to download from your own OneDrive. This is ignored when drive_id is provided.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The ID of the drive containing the file. Required for SharePoint or OneDrive for Business drives. When provided, user_id is ignored.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the file. Use this when downloading files from SharePoint sites or specific OneDrive for Business drives.

file_name.title: File Name
file_name.description: Desired filename (including extension) for the downloaded content.
file_name.human_parameter_description: The name you want to give the downloaded file, including its extension (like .docx or .png), so it saves with the right name on your device.

if_none_match.title: If None Match
if_none_match.description: Optional ETag or cTag value for conditional download. If the provided tag matches the current file's tag, the API returns HTTP 304 Not Modified without downloading the file, saving bandwidth. Useful for caching scenarios.
if_none_match.human_parameter_description: Provide an ETag or cTag value to avoid re-downloading the file if it hasn't changed. The download will be skipped if the file's current tag matches this value.

tools.name: Format Workbook Range
tools.description: Apply dimensions, alignment, wrapping, font, fill, and borders to a workbook range. Components are updated sequentially, not atomically, so earlier formatting remains if a later update fails.

font.title: RangeFontPatch

size.title: Size

color.title: Color
color.description: HTML named color or hexadecimal #RRGGBB font color.

underline.title: FontUnderline

color.title: Color

side_index.title: Side Index

borders.title: Borders

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: DriveItem ID of the Office Open XML workbook.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Workbook session ID returned by ONE_DRIVE_CREATE_WORKBOOK_SESSION.

base_format.title: BaseRangeFormatPatch

wrapText.title: Wrap Text
wrapText.description: Whether text in the range should wrap.

rowHeight.title: Row Height
rowHeight.description: Height to apply to every row in the range, in points.

columnWidth.title: Column Width
columnWidth.description: Width to apply to every column in the range, in points.

verticalAlignment.title: VerticalAlignment
verticalAlignment.description: Vertical alignment to apply to the range.

horizontalAlignment.title: HorizontalAlignment
horizontalAlignment.description: Horizontal alignment to apply to the range.

base_format.description: Optional dimensions, alignment, and wrapping changes.

worksheet_id_or_name.title: Worksheet Id Or Name
worksheet_id_or_name.description: Worksheet ID or exact worksheet name containing the range.

tools.name: Get Drive
tools.description: Retrieves the properties and relationships of a Drive resource by its unique ID. Use this action when you need to get details about a specific OneDrive, user's OneDrive, group's document library, or a site's document library. Only drives accessible to the authenticated user are returned; missing drives indicate insufficient OAuth scope or tenant permissions.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. This can be the ID of the user's personal OneDrive, a group's document library, or a specific drive ID. Must be a valid, non-empty value; use ONE_DRIVE_LIST_DRIVES to obtain valid drive IDs.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The drive you want to look up. Use 'me' for your own OneDrive, or provide a specific drive ID or a reference like users/{user}, groups/{group}, or sites/{site}.

expand_fields.title: Expand Fields
expand_fields.description: A comma-separated list of relationships to expand and include in the response. For example, "root,list" to include the root folder and list information. This allows you to retrieve related resources in a single request.
expand_fields.human_parameter_description: Include related details with the drive, such as root folder or list info. Enter relationships to expand (e.g., root, list).

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: A comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. Use this to retrieve specific fields and reduce the response size. For example, "id,name,driveType". If not provided, all default properties are returned.
select_fields.human_parameter_description: Pick the specific drive properties you want to return (e.g., id, name, driveType). This helps keep the response smaller; leave empty to get the default fields.

tools.name: Get DriveItem by Sharing URL
tools.description: Tool to resolve a OneDrive/SharePoint sharing URL (or shareId) to a DriveItem with driveId and itemId. Use when you have a sharing link from Teams, chat, or 1drv.ms and need the item's metadata or IDs for downstream actions like permissions or download.

sharing_url.title: Sharing Url
sharing_url.description: A OneDrive or SharePoint sharing URL (e.g., 1drv.ms link, SharePoint link, or Teams contentUrl). This will be automatically encoded to a sharing token. Mutually exclusive with share_id_or_encoded_url.

prefer_redeem.title: Prefer Redeem
prefer_redeem.description: Controls access redemption. 'redeemSharingLink' grants durable access to the item. 'redeemSharingLinkIfNecessary' grants access only for this request. If not specified, no Prefer header is sent.

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: A list of DriveItem properties to return. If not specified, a default set of properties is returned. Common fields: id, name, size, webUrl, file, folder, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, parentReference.

expand_children.title: Expand Children
expand_children.description: If true and the item is a folder, expands the children collection to include child items in the response.

share_id_or_encoded_url.title: Share Id Or Encoded Url
share_id_or_encoded_url.description: An already-encoded sharing token (prefixed with 'u!') or a shareId token from a previous API call. Mutually exclusive with sharing_url.

tools.name: Get Drives Following
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific followed driveItem from a drive. Use when you need to get details about a file or folder that the user has marked to follow.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. This can be the ID of the user's personal OneDrive, a group's document library, or a specific drive ID.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the OneDrive or SharePoint drive containing the followed item. You can get this from a previous drive listing operation.

drive_item_id.title: Drive Item Id
drive_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the followed driveItem to retrieve. This is the ID of a specific file or folder that has been followed.
drive_item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the specific file or folder that is being followed. You can get this from the list of followed items.

tools.name: Get Group Drive
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the document library (drive) for a Microsoft 365 group. Use when you need to access the default document library associated with a specific group.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of the group whose document library you want to retrieve.

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: A list of properties to include in the response. Use this to retrieve specific fields and reduce the response size. For example, ["id", "name", "driveType"]. If not provided, all default properties are returned.

tools.name: Get Item Metadata
tools.description: Retrieves the metadata of a DriveItem by its unique ID. Use this tool to get information about a specific file or folder in OneDrive when you have its ID. If a `drive_id` is not provided, it defaults to the user's main drive.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the DriveItem (file or folder). DriveItem IDs vary by platform: OneDrive for Business/SharePoint uses '01...' prefix format (e.g., '01NKDM7HMOJTVYMDOSXFDK2QJDXCDI3WUK'), while OneDrive Personal uses 'HASH!NUMBER' format (e.g., 'D4648F06C91D9D3D!54927'). IDs are case-sensitive and must be used exactly as returned from Microsoft Graph API. Obtain IDs from ONE_DRIVE_LIST_FOLDER_CHILDREN, ONE_DRIVE_SEARCH_ITEMS, or similar operations. Do NOT use: web URLs, sharing links, SharePoint listItem IDs, or manually constructed identifiers. IDs become stale after move, rename, or delete; refresh via ONE_DRIVE_SEARCH_ITEMS or ONE_DRIVE_LIST_FOLDER_CHILDREN instead of retrying a stale ID.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the file or folder you want to retrieve. Use the ID exactly as returned from a previous list, search, or folder listing operation. IDs are case-sensitive. Do NOT use URLs, sharing links, or IDs from other systems.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the Drive where the item is located. If not provided, the action will target the user's personal OneDrive (me/drive). Always specify drive_id explicitly for group drives, SharePoint site drives, or shared libraries to avoid silently querying the wrong drive.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The OneDrive or SharePoint drive where the item is stored. Leave this blank to use your own OneDrive.

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: A list of DriveItem properties to return. If not specified, a default set of properties is returned. Refer to the DriveItem resource documentation for available fields.
select_fields.human_parameter_description: Choose which details you want returned about the item (for example: id, name, size). Leave empty to get the usual default details.

items.title: ExpandableRelation
items.description: Valid navigation properties that can be expanded for a driveItem.

expand_relations.title: Expand Relations
expand_relations.description: Navigation properties to expand in the response. Valid values: 'children' (folder contents), 'thumbnails' (image previews), 'versions' (version history), 'permissions' (sharing permissions), 'listItem' (SharePoint list item data), 'activities' (recent activities), 'analytics' (usage analytics), 'createdByUser' (creator user details), 'lastModifiedByUser' (last modifier user details), 'retentionLabel' (retention policy), 'subscriptions' (webhooks), 'workbook' (Excel workbook data). Note: 'content' is NOT expandable - use ONE_DRIVE_DOWNLOAD_FILE to retrieve file content; 'listItem' requires SharePoint drives; some properties have regional/license restrictions. When expanding 'children': the array may be empty or absent; check for its presence and branch on 'file' vs 'folder' facets before processing. Expansion is non-recursive — call this tool separately for each child folder to traverse nested trees.
expand_relations.human_parameter_description: Include related information in the result. Common: 'children' (folder contents), 'thumbnails' (previews), 'versions' (history), 'permissions' (sharing). Note: 'content' cannot be expanded - use ONE_DRIVE_DOWNLOAD_FILE to get file content instead.

tools.name: Get Item Permissions
tools.description: Retrieves the permissions of a DriveItem by its unique ID within a specific Drive. Use when you need to check who has access to a file or folder and what level of access they have. Response nests permission entries under `data.value`; check top-level `success`/`error` flags before processing results. Results include inherited permissions, owner entries, and anonymous link entries — not just explicitly granted permissions. Sharing links may have differing scopes (org-only vs. anonymous); verify `link.scope` before treating a permission as externally accessible.

select.title: Select
select.description: A comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. For example, 'id,roles,link'.
select.human_parameter_description: Pick which fields you want returned to keep the response focused (e.g., 'id,roles,link').

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item. Verify the correct item before calling — disambiguate similarly named files using folder path, timestamps, or file size. Required unless item_path is provided.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the file or folder you want to check. Use this when you know the item’s ID; otherwise, you can use Item Path instead.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of a SharePoint site. Use this if the item is in a SharePoint site's drive.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the SharePoint site where the item is stored. Use this when the file or folder is in a SharePoint document library.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of a user. Use this if the item is in a specific user's drive (other than 'me').
user_id.human_parameter_description: The identifier (email or GUID) of the user whose OneDrive contains the item. Use this when the item is in someone else’s drive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. Required if not using other identifiers like group_id, site_id, or user_id in the path.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the drive that contains the file or folder you’re checking. Provide this if you know the exact drive or aren’t using a group, site, or user ID.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of a group. Use this if the item is in a group's drive.
group_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the Microsoft 365 group whose drive contains the item. Use this if the file or folder is stored in a group drive.

item_path.title: Item Path
item_path.description: The path to the item relative to the drive's root. Use this if item_id is not known. Must start with ':/' and end with ':/'. Example: ':/FolderA/FileB.txt:/'. Only applicable when accessing items in the current user's drive (me/drive/root). Does NOT substitute `item_id` (which is required); use only as supplemental path context for items in the current user's drive.
item_path.human_parameter_description: The location of the file or folder within the drive, for example ':/FolderA/FileB.txt:/'. Use this when you don’t know the Item ID.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifiers, but filter/sort params need not be repeated — the token carries them.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Leave blank for the first page. To get the next page, paste the page token from the previous response.

if_none_match.title: If None Match
if_none_match.description: If this request header value (etag) matches the current etag on the item, an HTTP 304 Not Modified response is returned.
if_none_match.human_parameter_description: Optional ETag value for caching. If the ETag matches, the API returns 304 Not Modified to save bandwidth.

tools.name: Get Item Thumbnails
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the thumbnails associated with a DriveItem. Use when you need to display visual previews of files. Response contains a `value` array with size keys (`small`, `medium`, `large`); thumbnails may not be generated for all file types or newly uploaded items, so handle an empty or missing `value` array. Returned thumbnail URLs are external HTTP endpoints with independent availability.

select.title: Select
select.description: A comma-separated list of thumbnail sizes to retrieve (e.g., "small,medium,large", or "c300x400_crop"). If not specified, all available thumbnails for the first thumbnailSet (id: "0") are returned.
select.human_parameter_description: List the thumbnail sizes you want returned (e.g., small, medium, large, or a custom size like c300x400_crop). Leave empty to return all available sizes.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the DriveItem.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the file or item whose thumbnails you want to fetch. You can copy this from a previous file listing or search.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of a Site. Provide either drive_id, group_id, site_id, or user_id.
site_id.human_parameter_description: Use this if the item is in a SharePoint site. Paste the Site ID so we can find it in that site's drive.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of a User. Provide either drive_id, group_id, site_id, or user_id.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Use this to target another user's OneDrive. Enter that user's ID; leave blank to use your own drive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the Drive. If not provided, 'me' will be used for the current user's drive.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: Specify which drive the item lives in. Leave blank to use your own OneDrive, or paste a specific Drive ID to target another drive.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of a Group. Provide either drive_id, group_id, site_id, or user_id.
group_id.human_parameter_description: Use this if the item is stored in a Microsoft 365 Group drive. Enter the Group’s ID so we look in the right place.

original_orientation.title: Original Orientation
original_orientation.description: If true, retrieves the thumbnail with its original EXIF orientation. This is only supported on OneDrive Personal. Defaults to false.
original_orientation.human_parameter_description: Choose whether thumbnails should keep the photo’s original camera orientation. Turn this on if your images appear rotated; this only works for personal OneDrive.

tools.name: Get Item Versions
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the version history of a DriveItem by its unique ID. Use when you need to access or list previous versions of a file. Version history may be unavailable or empty for folders or items in drives without versioning enabled.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the item (file or folder).
item_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the file or folder whose version history you want to view. Use the ID you got from a previous file lookup or from the item’s details link.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the site. Mutually exclusive with drive_id, group_id, and user_id.
site_id.human_parameter_description: Use this when the item is in a SharePoint site’s drive. Enter the site’s ID, and don’t provide Drive ID, Group ID, or User ID at the same time.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user. Mutually exclusive with drive_id, group_id, and site_id.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Use this when the item is in a specific user’s OneDrive. Enter that user’s ID; leave blank to use your own account or provide one of the other location options instead.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. Mutually exclusive with group_id, site_id, and user_id. One of these must be provided if not using the /me path.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: Provide this if the item is in a specific OneDrive or SharePoint drive and you know its ID. Only fill one of Drive ID, Group ID, Site ID, or User ID.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of the group. Mutually exclusive with drive_id, site_id, and user_id.
group_id.human_parameter_description: Use this when the item lives in a Microsoft 365 Group’s drive. Enter the group’s ID, and don’t provide Drive ID, Site ID, or User ID at the same time.

tools.name: Get Recent Items
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Microsoft has deprecated the `GET /me/drive/recent` endpoint backing this action; it already runs in a degraded state and stops returning data after November 2026. This action is retained for backward compatibility and will be removed once the upstream API is fully retired. Get files and folders recently accessed by the user. Returns items based on activity history (opened, edited, viewed), sorted by most recent first — NOT by modification time; use ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_LIST_ITEMS or ONE_DRIVE_LIST_ROOT_DRIVE_CHANGES for strictly modification-based queries. Use when you need to see what the user worked on recently (e.g., 'Show me files I worked on today'). Different from search - this tracks activity, not content. Results may contain duplicate names; disambiguate using lastModifiedDateTime, parentReference.path, and the file/folder property before acting on a specific item.

top.title: Top
top.description: Maximum number of recent items to return (1-200). Controls response size for better performance. Use pagination with @odata.nextLink for larger datasets.
top.human_parameter_description: How many recent files and folders you want to see (1-200). Choose a smaller number for faster, more focused results.

select.title: Select
select.description: Comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. Significantly reduces payload size by returning only specified fields. Common properties: id, name, webUrl, size, lastModifiedDateTime, lastAccessedDateTime, file, folder, parentReference. If not specified, all properties are returned (large payload). Always include id in select and use returned id values directly — never reconstruct or hardcode IDs, as stale or manually constructed IDs will fail in tools like ONE_DRIVE_GET_ITEM.
select.human_parameter_description: Which details to return for each item (for example: id, name, web link, size). Choosing fewer fields makes the response faster and easier to scan.

tools.name: Get Drive Root Folder
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata for the root folder of the signed-in user's OneDrive. Use when you need information about the user's OneDrive root directory, such as size, child count, or web URL.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's ID, email, or 'me'. Defaults to 'me' (authenticated user). Required for S2S (app-only) auth.

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: A list of properties to include in the response. Use this to retrieve specific fields and reduce the response size. Common fields include: id, name, size, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, webUrl, folder, root. If not provided, all default properties are returned.

tools.name: Get Shared Items
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use ONE_DRIVE_SEARCH_DRIVE_ITEMS to find a specific shared file or ONE_DRIVE_LIST_ONEDRIVE_SHARED_ITEMS to list files shared from other people's OneDrive accounts. Microsoft Graph sharedWithMe is degraded until November 2026 and will stop returning data after that.

allow_external.title: Allow External
allow_external.description: Set to true to include items shared from external tenants. Defaults to false, which only returns items shared within the user's own tenant.
allow_external.human_parameter_description: Choose whether to include items shared by people outside your organization. Turn this on to see files and folders shared from external tenants; leave it off to show only items shared within your own tenant.

tools.name: Get SharePoint List Items
tools.description: Tool to get the items (list items) within a specific SharePoint list on a site. Use when you need to retrieve data from a SharePoint list.

top.title: Top
top.description: The maximum number of items to return in a single response. Used for pagination.
top.human_parameter_description: Limit the number of items returned per page. Use this to control paging and avoid very large responses.

skip.title: Skip
skip.description: The number of items to skip in the result set. Used for pagination.
skip.human_parameter_description: Skip a certain number of items before returning results. Useful for pagination when combined with top.

count.title: Count
count.description: If true, returns the total count of items in the @odata.count property.
count.human_parameter_description: Set to true to include the total number of items in the response.

expand.title: Expand
expand.description: A comma-separated list of relationships to expand, or 'fields($select=columnName1,columnName2)' to retrieve specific fields. For example, to get specific columns 'Name' and 'Color', use 'fields($select=Name,Color)'. SharePoint internal field names may differ from display names; call without expand first (or use 'fields' alone) to discover actual internal names before filtering or selecting specific fields.
expand.human_parameter_description: Optionally include related details or choose specific columns to return. For example, use fields(select=Name,Color) to fetch only those columns.

filter.title: Filter
filter.description: An OData filter query to restrict the results. For example, to filter items where 'Quantity' is less than 600, use 'fields/Quantity lt 600'.
filter.human_parameter_description: Return only items that match a condition, such as fields/Quantity lt 600. Use this when you want a focused subset instead of all items.

select.title: Select
select.description: A comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. Often used in conjunction with '$expand=fields(select=...)'. For example, 'id,name,fields'.
select.human_parameter_description: Choose which top-level properties to include in the results (for example: id,name,fields). This helps keep the response concise and relevant.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The unique identifier of the list within the SharePoint site.
list_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the specific list you want to read items from within the site. Use the list's GUID for the list you want to query.

orderby.title: Orderby
orderby.description: OData order by expression to sort results. For example, 'fields/Name asc' or 'fields/Quantity desc'.
orderby.human_parameter_description: Choose how to sort the results. For example, sort by a field name ascending or descending.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the SharePoint site.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The identifier of the SharePoint site that contains your list. This tells us which site to read items from.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifiers, but filter/sort params need not be repeated — the token carries them.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Leave blank for the first page. To get the next page, paste the page token from the previous response.

tools.name: Get Site Details
tools.description: Retrieves metadata for a specific SharePoint site by its ID. Use this action when you need to get details like display name, web URL, and creation/modification dates for a known SharePoint site.

expand.title: Expand
expand.description: Comma-separated list of relationships to expand in the response. Example: columns,lists,drives
expand.human_parameter_description: Include related details for the site, such as columns, lists, or drives. Provide a comma-separated list like columns,lists.

select.title: Select
select.description: Comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. Example: id,displayName,webUrl
select.human_parameter_description: Choose which properties to return for the site to keep results concise. Provide a comma-separated list like id,displayName,webUrl.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the SharePoint site. This is the id property of the site resource.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the SharePoint site you want details for. Paste the site ID from SharePoint or a previous site search; it often looks like 'contoso.sharepoint.com,GUID,GUID'.

tools.name: Get SharePoint Site Page Content
tools.description: Gets the content of a modern SharePoint site page. Use when you need to retrieve the details and content of a specific page within a SharePoint site.

expand.title: Expand
expand.description: Expands related entities. For example, use 'canvasLayout' to include the page's layout and web part content.
expand.human_parameter_description: Optional: include extra details about the page in the results—for example, use 'canvasLayout' to include the page layout and web parts.

select.title: Select
select.description: Comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. Example: id,name,title
select.human_parameter_description: Optional: choose which properties to return for the page. Provide a comma-separated list like id,name,title to get only those fields.

page_id.title: Page Id
page_id.description: The unique identifier of the site page.
page_id.human_parameter_description: The specific page you want to retrieve. Provide the page’s unique ID; you can get it from a page list or a previous search.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the SharePoint site.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The SharePoint site that contains the page. Paste the site's ID so we know exactly which site to read from (you can copy it from a previous site lookup or your admin center).

tools.name: Get User Profile
tools.description: Retrieves the properties and profile information for a specific Microsoft user by their user ID or user principal name. Use this action when you need to get detailed information about a user's profile, including their contact details, job information, and account status. This action requires the User.Read or User.ReadBasic.All OAuth scope to access user profile data.

select.title: Select
select.description: Specific properties to return in the response. Use this to retrieve only the fields you need and reduce response size. Example properties: displayName, mail, jobTitle, givenName, surname, mobilePhone. If not provided, all default user properties are returned.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user principal name (UPN) or user ID to retrieve. Examples: 'user@contoso.com' or '87d349ed-44d7-43e1-9a83-5f2406dee5bd'. This is a required parameter that identifies which user's profile to fetch.

tools.name: Grant Shares Permission
tools.description: Tool to grant users access to a link represented by a permission using an encoded sharing URL. Use when you need to give specific users access to a shared OneDrive or SharePoint resource.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Array of Microsoft Graph role strings specifying the access level to grant. Documented/common values include 'read' and 'write'; permission resources may also use 'owner' for SharePoint/OneDrive for Business where supported, and tenant/resource-specific roles may also be accepted by Graph.
roles.human_parameter_description: The permission level(s) to grant, such as 'read', 'write', 'owner' where supported, or another Microsoft Graph-supported role for the resource.

email.title: Email
email.description: The email address of the recipient to grant access.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.description: Array of recipient objects with email addresses who will receive access to the shared link.
recipients.human_parameter_description: List of people (by email) who will be granted access to the shared resource.

encoded_sharing_url.title: Encoded Sharing Url
encoded_sharing_url.description: Base64url encoded sharing URL (must be prefixed with u!). Encode the sharing URL using base64url format and prefix with 'u!' to create the encoded sharing URL.
encoded_sharing_url.human_parameter_description: The encoded version of the sharing URL. Must be base64url encoded and prefixed with 'u!'. This represents the shared resource you want to grant access to.

tools.name: Grant SharePoint Item Permission
tools.description: Grant an application permission on a SharePoint list or list item using Microsoft Graph beta.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Roles to grant to the application, such as read or write.
roles.human_parameter_description: The access level to grant, for example read or write.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: Optional SharePoint list item ID. Provide this to grant permission on a list item; omit it to grant permission on the list.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The list item ID when granting list-item permission. Leave empty for list-level permissions.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The unique Microsoft Graph ID of the SharePoint list.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The Microsoft Graph SharePoint site ID in composite format, usually 'hostname,site-collection-id,web-id'.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The SharePoint site ID containing the list or list item.

granted_to_v2.title: Granted To V2

application.title: Application

id.title: Id
id.description: The Microsoft Entra application ID to grant SharePoint permission to.

displayName.title: Display Name
displayName.description: Optional display name of the application.

application.description: The application identity to grant access to. Microsoft Graph beta list/listItem permission APIs do not create user permissions.

granted_to_v2.description: Application identity to grant access to. Microsoft Graph beta does not create user permissions on list or list-item resources.

tools.name: Inspect Workbook Table
tools.description: Read a workbook table's occupied range and one page of its columns.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: DriveItem ID of the Office Open XML workbook.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: Drive containing the workbook. Use 'me' for the connected user's drive, or provide a Microsoft Graph drive ID.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque token for the next columns page. Omit initially, then pass next_page_token back unchanged.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Optional workbook session ID to use for both table reads.

column_page_size.title: Column Page Size
column_page_size.description: Maximum columns to request on the first page. Microsoft Graph may return fewer.

table_id_or_name.title: Table Id Or Name
table_id_or_name.description: Exact table ID or table name in the workbook.

tools.name: Invite User to Drive Item
tools.description: Tool to invite users or grant permissions to a specific item in a OneDrive drive. Use when you need to share a file or folder with other users and define their access level (e.g., read or write).

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Specifies the roles to be granted to the recipients. Microsoft Graph accepts a string array; documented/common values include 'read' and 'write'; permission resources may also use 'owner' for SharePoint/OneDrive for Business, and Graph may accept tenant/resource-specific role strings.
roles.human_parameter_description: Provide one or more Microsoft Graph permission roles. Start with 'read' or 'write'; use 'owner' only where the target SharePoint/OneDrive for Business permission supports it, or other Graph-supported tenant/resource-specific role strings.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item (file or folder).
item_id.human_parameter_description: The specific file or folder you want to share. Paste its item ID from the link or from a previous list/search step.

message.title: Message
message.description: A plain text formatted message that is included in the sharing invitation. Maximum length 2000 characters.
message.human_parameter_description: A short note to include in the invitation email, such as context, instructions, or a friendly message.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of a SharePoint site. Use this if the item is in a SharePoint site's drive.
site_id.human_parameter_description: If the item is in a SharePoint site's drive, provide that site's ID so we know where to look.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of a user. Use this if the item is in another user's drive that you have access to.
user_id.human_parameter_description: If the item is in another user's OneDrive that you can access, enter that user's ID to target their drive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. If not provided, the authenticated user's personal drive (me/drive) will be used.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: Which drive the item is in. Leave blank to use your own drive, or provide a specific drive ID if the file is elsewhere.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of a Microsoft 365 group. Use this if the item is in a group's drive.
group_id.human_parameter_description: If the item is in a Microsoft 365 group's drive, enter that group's ID so the item can be found.

password.title: Password
password.description: The password set on the invite by the creator. Optional and OneDrive Personal only.
password.human_parameter_description: An optional password recipients must enter to open the shared link. Use this to add an extra layer of security.

alias.title: Alias
alias.description: The alias of the recipient, if a personal Microsoft Account.

email.title: Email
email.description: The email address of the recipient.

object_id.title: Object Id
object_id.description: The object ID of the recipient, if a user or group in Azure AD.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.description: A collection of recipients who will receive access and the sharing invitation.
recipients.human_parameter_description: Who you want to share with. Add one or more people (typically by email) to grant them access.

require_sign_in.title: Require Sign In
require_sign_in.description: Specifies whether the recipient of the invitation is required to sign-in to view the shared item. At least one of require_sign_in or send_invitation must be true.
require_sign_in.human_parameter_description: Require recipients to sign in before opening the item. Keep this on to ensure only the intended people can access it.

send_invitation.title: Send Invitation
send_invitation.description: If true, a sharing link is sent to the recipient. Otherwise, a permission is granted directly without sending a notification.
send_invitation.human_parameter_description: Decide whether to send an email invitation to recipients. Turn this on to notify them by email or off to grant access silently.

expiration_date_time.title: Expiration Date Time
expiration_date_time.description: Specifies the dateTime after which the permission expires. ISO 8601 format. Example: "2023-12-31T23:59:59.000Z"
expiration_date_time.human_parameter_description: When the granted access should expire. Set a date and time to automatically remove access after that moment.

retain_inherited_permissions.title: Retain Inherited Permissions
retain_inherited_permissions.description: Optional. If true (default), any existing inherited permissions are retained on the shared item when sharing this item for the first time. If false, all existing permissions are removed when sharing for the first time.
retain_inherited_permissions.human_parameter_description: Whether to keep existing permissions on the item when sharing. Turn off to remove old access and only keep the new permissions.

tools.name: List Drive Activities
tools.description: Tool to retrieve recent activities on the authenticated user's OneDrive. Use when you need to track recent changes or actions performed across the drive.

input.title: ListActivitiesRequest

top.title: Top
top.description: The maximum number of activities to return. Must be between 1 and 999.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
