Format: {"id": "<folder-id>", "driveId": "<drive-id>"} (driveId is optional). Example: {"id": "01BYE5RZZ272Y2AM3L22L22Z2Y2Y2Y2Y2Y"}. Note: Folder names are not accepted - use the folder's unique ID obtained from listing or searching items.
parentReference.human_parameter_description: The destination folder for the item. Must be an object with the folder's unique ID, e.g., {"id": "folder-id-here"}. The ID can be obtained by listing folder contents or searching for items. Folder names (display names) are not accepted.

tools.name: Create folder
tools.description: Creates a new folder in the user's OneDrive with configurable conflict behavior, optionally within a specified parent_folder (by ID or full path from root) which, if not the root, must exist and be accessible.

name.title: Name
name.description: The desired name for the new folder (also accepts 'folder_name' as an alias). If a folder with this name already exists in the specified parent_folder, the new folder will be automatically renamed (e.g., 'New Folder' might become 'New Folder 1'). Examples: ['Annual Reports', 'Client Meeting Notes']
name.human_parameter_description: The name you want to give the new folder. If that name already exists in the chosen location, we'll add a number to make it unique.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's ID, email, or 'me'. Defaults to 'me' (authenticated user). Required for S2S (app-only) auth.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the OneDrive account to use. Enter 'me' to use your own account.

description.title: Description
description.description: Optional description for the folder. Provides a user-visible description of the folder. Examples: ['Project documents for Q1 2024', 'Meeting notes archive']
description.human_parameter_description: An optional description or summary for the folder to help others understand its purpose.

parent_folder.title: Parent Folder
parent_folder.description: ID or full path of the parent folder for the new folder. Paths must start from the root (e.g., '/Documents/Reports'). If an ID is provided, it refers to an existing folder's unique ID. Examples: ['/Projects/Alpha', 'folder_id_12345ABC', '/']
parent_folder.human_parameter_description: Where you want to create the new folder. Provide a full path from the root (like '/Documents/Reports'), a specific folder ID, or use '/' for the root.

conflict_behavior.title: Conflict Behavior
conflict_behavior.description: How Microsoft Graph should handle a folder name conflict in the target parent folder. Use 'fail' to return an error, 'rename' to create a uniquely renamed folder, or 'replace' to replace the existing item when supported by Graph.
conflict_behavior.human_parameter_description: Choose what to do if a folder with the same name already exists: fail, rename, or replace. Defaults to rename for backward compatibility.

tools.name: Create a new text file
tools.description: Creates a new plain-text file with specified content in the authenticated user's personal OneDrive, using either the folder's unique ID or its absolute path relative to the user's OneDrive root (paths are automatically resolved to IDs); note that OneDrive may rename or create a new version if the filename already exists. All files are written as plain text regardless of extension — specifying .docx or .xlsx does not produce a true Office document. This action only works with the user's personal OneDrive (/me/drive) and does not support SharePoint document libraries or shared drives.

name.title: Name
name.description: The desired name for the new text file, including its extension (e.g., 'report.txt', 'notes.log'). Also accepts 'file_name' as an alias.
name.human_parameter_description: The exact name you want for the new text file, including the extension (e.g., 'notes.txt'). This is how it will appear in OneDrive.

folder.title: Folder
folder.description: The folder within the user's personal OneDrive where the new text file will be created. Use '/' for root, a path like '/Documents/Projects' (relative to OneDrive root), a folder name like 'MyFolder' (treated as '/MyFolder'), or a valid folder ID. Note: Paths are resolved against the user's personal OneDrive (/me/drive/root) only and cannot target SharePoint document libraries or shared drives.
folder.human_parameter_description: The folder in your personal OneDrive where you want to create the new file. You can enter a path like '/Documents/Projects' (relative to your OneDrive root), a folder name like 'MyFolder', or a folder ID; use '/' for your OneDrive root. Note: This only works with your personal OneDrive, not SharePoint sites.

content.title: Content
examples: This is the content of the new text file.
TODO: Finalize the project proposal by EOD.
content.description: The plain text content to be written into the new file. For very large text bodies, the request may fail or truncate; split large content across multiple files if needed.
content.human_parameter_description: The text to store in the file. Paste or type the content exactly as you want it saved.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's ID or the literal 'me' to represent the currently authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or ID of the OneDrive user whose drive you want to use. Enter 'me' to use your own OneDrive.

conflict_behavior.title: Conflict Behavior
conflict_behavior.description: How to handle conflicts when a file with the same name already exists. 'fail' (default) returns an error if the file exists, 'replace' overwrites the existing file, 'rename' creates a new file with an incremented name (e.g., 'file 1.txt').
conflict_behavior.human_parameter_description: What to do if a file with this name already exists: 'fail' will show an error, 'replace' will overwrite the existing file, or 'rename' will create a new file with a number added to the name.

tools.name: Preview Drive Item
tools.description: Generates or retrieves a short-lived, permission-bound embeddable URL for a preview of a specific item. URLs expire and must be regenerated per session — do not cache. Use when you need to display a temporary preview of a file.

page.title: Page
page.description: Optional. Page number of document to start at, if applicable. Specified as string for future use cases around file types such as ZIP.
page.human_parameter_description: Start the preview on a specific page of the document. Enter a page number (like 1) or a label if the file uses named pages.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Optional. Zoom level to start at, if applicable.
zoom.human_parameter_description: Set the initial zoom level for the preview. Use 1.0 for 100%, 0.5 for 50%, 2.0 for 200%, etc.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the DriveItem.
item_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the ID of the file you want to preview so we can generate a preview link. You can copy this from the file's details, URL, or a previous list/search step.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the Site. Provide if the item is in a SharePoint site.
site_id.human_parameter_description: If the file is stored in a SharePoint site, enter that site's ID so we search that site's drive. Skip if the item is in OneDrive.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of the User. Provide if the item is in another user's drive.
user_id.human_parameter_description: If the file is in another person's OneDrive, enter that user's ID to look in their drive. Leave blank to use your own drive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the Drive. If not provided, the request will be made to the current user's drive.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: If the file is in a specific drive (like a shared drive), enter that drive's ID so we look in the right place. Leave blank to use your own drive by default.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of the Group. Provide if the item is in a group drive.
group_id.human_parameter_description: If the file is in a Microsoft 365 Group's drive, enter that Group ID so we can find it. Skip this unless you know the item is in a group drive.

share_id.title: Share Id
share_id.description: The unique identifier of the shared item. Provide if the item is accessed via a share link.
share_id.human_parameter_description: If you're accessing the item via a sharing link, paste the share ID here so we can resolve it. Use this when you have a sharing link instead of a direct drive path.

tools.name: Read Workbook Range
tools.description: Reads a range of cells from an Excel workbook worksheet stored in OneDrive or SharePoint using Microsoft Graph API. Returns cell values, formulas, formatting, and metadata for the specified range. Use this action when you need to extract data from specific cells in an Excel file, whether reading a single cell, a rectangular range, an entire column, or an entire row. The range address must be specified in A1 notation (e.g., 'A1:B5').

address.title: Address
address.description: The range address in A1 notation. Supports single cells (e.g., 'A1'), cell ranges (e.g., 'A1:B5'), entire columns (e.g., 'A:A'), or entire rows (e.g., '1:1'). The address is used as-is in the Graph API function call syntax.
address.human_parameter_description: The cell range to read in Excel notation (e.g., 'A1:B5' for a rectangular range, 'A1' for a single cell, or 'A:A' for an entire column).

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the workbook item (Excel file). This is the DriveItem ID for the Excel file containing the worksheet you want to read from.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the Excel file. Get this from file listing or search operations.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the workbook. Required to locate the Excel file in OneDrive or SharePoint.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the OneDrive or SharePoint drive where the Excel workbook is stored. Get this from a previous list drives operation.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Optional workbook session ID. Use this to read from an existing Excel workbook session.

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: Optional list of specific fields to return in the response. If not specified, all default range properties are returned. Available fields include: address, addressLocal, cellCount, columnCount, columnHidden, columnIndex, hidden, rowCount, rowHidden, rowIndex, values, formulas, text, valueTypes, numberFormat.
select_fields.human_parameter_description: Optionally choose which specific properties to return (e.g., just 'values' and 'text'). Leave blank to get all properties.

worksheet_id_or_name.title: Worksheet Id Or Name
worksheet_id_or_name.description: The ID or name of the worksheet within the workbook. Can be a worksheet name like 'Sheet1' or a worksheet ID like '{00000000-0001-0000-0000-000000000000}'. Non-ASCII names are automatically URL-encoded.
worksheet_id_or_name.human_parameter_description: The name or ID of the specific worksheet tab in the workbook where the range is located.

tools.name: Restore Deleted Item
tools.description: Tool to restore a deleted OneDrive driveItem (file or folder) from the recycle bin. Use when you need to recover a deleted item to its original location or to a specified parent folder, optionally renaming it during restoration. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: This API is ONLY available for OneDrive Personal accounts. It does NOT work with OneDrive for Business or SharePoint. For Business/SharePoint accounts, use the SharePoint REST API endpoints (/_api/web/recyclebin) instead.

name.title: Name
name.description: (Optional) The new name for the restored item. If not provided, the item will be restored with its original name. This is useful if you want to rename the item during the restore process or if an item with the same name already exists in the destination.
name.human_parameter_description: Optional: Enter a new name for the restored item. Leave empty to keep the original name.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the deleted DriveItem (file or folder) to restore. This item must currently be in the OneDrive recycle bin. The ID can be obtained from deleted items listing or from the item before deletion.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the deleted file or folder you want to restore from the recycle bin. Use the ID from when the item was deleted or from a deleted items listing.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the Drive containing the deleted item. Required when using application authentication. If not provided with delegated authentication, uses the authenticated user's default drive.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the drive containing the deleted item. Required for application authentication or when accessing items in a specific drive.

parent_reference_id.title: Parent Reference Id
parent_reference_id.description: (Optional) The unique identifier of the parent folder where the item should be restored. If not provided, the item will be restored to its original parent location. This is useful when you want to restore the item to a different folder than where it was originally located.
parent_reference_id.human_parameter_description: Optional: The ID of the folder where you want to restore the item. Leave empty to restore to the original location.

tools.name: Restore Item Version
tools.description: Restores a previous version of a DriveItem (file) by creating a new version with the content of the specified version. Use this action when you need to revert a file to an earlier version. The restoration is permanent and creates a new current version — the file cannot be automatically reverted after this operation, though you can restore again to a different version if needed. This action is irreversible in the sense that it immediately changes the current file content.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the DriveItem (file) whose version you want to restore.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's ID, email, or 'me'. Defaults to 'me' (authenticated user) if not provided. Required for S2S (app-only) auth to specify target user.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the Drive where the item is located. If not provided, the action will target the user's personal OneDrive (me/drive). Always specify drive_id explicitly for group drives, SharePoint site drives, or shared libraries to avoid silently querying the wrong drive.

version_id.title: Version Id
version_id.description: The unique identifier of the version to restore. This creates a new version with the content of the specified previous version.

tools.name: Search Drive Items
tools.description: Search OneDrive and accessible SharePoint files with Microsoft Graph Search. This does not produce a complete shared-with-me list; use deprecated ONE_DRIVE_GET_SHARED_ITEMS only when full shared-with-me enumeration is required before Microsoft removes that API in November 2026. Requires OneDrive permissions plus Sites.Read.All because SharePoint-backed files can appear in results.

size.title: Size
size.description: Number of search results to return.

query.title: Query
query.description: Microsoft Search query for OneDrive and SharePoint driveItem results. KQL is supported. Use '*' to match all accessible drive items.
query.human_parameter_description: The keyword or KQL query to search across OneDrive and accessible SharePoint files.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Optional driveItem fields to return on each hit resource.

tools.name: Search Items
tools.description: Search OneDrive for files and folders by keyword. Searches filenames, metadata, and file content to find matching items. Use when you need to find specific files based on keywords, file types, or content. Supports filtering, sorting, and pagination. Results are mixed files and folders — filter client-side using file vs folder properties. Disambiguate similarly named items using parentReference.path, lastModifiedDateTime, and size before passing item IDs downstream. Newly created or recently moved files may not appear due to indexing delays; fall back to ONE_DRIVE_LIST_FOLDER_CHILDREN if expected items are missing. No server-side date filtering — apply lastModifiedDateTime/createdDateTime filtering in your own logic. HTTP 429 responses include a Retry-After header; use exponential backoff.

q.title: Q
q.description: The query text used to search for items. Values are matched across filenames, metadata, and file content. This is a simple keyword-based search only - NOT KQL (Keyword Query Language). IMPORTANT: (1) KQL operators like 'folder:', 'file:', 'content:', 'filetype:' are NOT supported by this endpoint and will be treated as literal text search. Use plain keywords instead (e.g., 'shared documents' not 'folder:shared'). (2) Path-based filtering syntax (e.g., 'path:/folder') is NOT supported and will be transformed to a keyword search. (3) Wildcard characters (* and ?) are NOT supported and will be automatically removed - use file extension keywords instead (e.g., 'mp4' instead of '*.mp4'). To search within a specific folder, use ONE_DRIVE_LIST_FOLDER_CHILDREN.
q.human_parameter_description: The words or phrase you want to search for in your OneDrive. Use keywords that appear in file names, content, or metadata. Note: KQL operators (folder:, file:, content:) and wildcards (* and ?) are not supported - use simple keywords like 'mp4' or 'shared documents' instead.

top.title: Top
top.description: The maximum number of items to return in a single page. Default is 200.
top.human_parameter_description: Limit how many results are returned per page. Set a smaller number to keep responses quick and manageable.

expand.title: Expand
expand.description: A comma-separated list of relationship names to expand and include in the response. For driveItem resources, you can expand relationships like 'children' to get child items, 'thumbnails' to get thumbnail metadata, or 'permissions' to get sharing permissions. For example, use 'children' to include the child items of folders in search results, or 'thumbnails' to include thumbnail URLs. Note: Not all relationships may be expandable in search results. Refer to the Microsoft Graph API documentation for supported expansions.
expand.human_parameter_description: Choose which related data to include in the results. For example, use 'children' to see contents of folders, 'thumbnails' for preview images, or 'permissions' for sharing details.

select.title: Select
select.description: Comma-separated list of driveItem properties to include in the response. Valid properties include: id, name, webUrl, size, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, file, folder, parentReference, createdBy, lastModifiedBy, fileSystemInfo, searchResult, remoteItem, etc. Note: @-prefixed annotations (e.g., @microsoft.graph.downloadUrl) are automatically stripped as they are not valid in $select queries for search endpoints.
select.human_parameter_description: Pick which details you want returned for each item to keep results focused. Enter a comma-separated list like 'id,name,webUrl'.

orderby.title: Orderby
orderby.description: A comma-separated list of properties used to sort the order of the items in the response. Use 'asc' or 'desc' for ascending or descending order, e.g., 'name asc'.
orderby.human_parameter_description: Choose how to sort the results. Specify the property and order, for example 'name asc' or 'name desc'.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The ID of the drive to search within. If not provided, the user's personal drive (me/drive) will be searched. Use ONE_DRIVE_LIST_DRIVES to get valid drive IDs. Note: Some drive ID formats (e.g., secondary personal drives or special SharePoint IDs) may return 'ObjectHandle is Invalid' errors due to Microsoft Graph API limitations.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: Choose which drive to search in. Leave blank to search your own OneDrive, or provide a specific drive, site, group, or user ID to target that location.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifiers, but filter/sort params need not be repeated — the token carries them.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Leave blank for the first page. To get the next page, paste the page token from the previous response.

search_scope.title: Search Scope
search_scope.description: Specifies the scope of the search. 'root' searches within the folder hierarchy starting from root (uses /drives/{drive_id}/root/search or /me/drive/root/search). 'drive' broadens the search to include items shared with the current user (uses /drives/{drive_id}/search or /me/drive/search). This parameter is respected both with and without a drive_id.
search_scope.human_parameter_description: Decide how broad the search should be. 'root' searches within a specific folder hierarchy, while 'drive' searches the whole drive, including items shared with you.

stripped_annotations.title: Stripped Annotations
stripped_annotations.description: Internal field to track stripped annotations. Not exposed to API.

transformed_path_query.title: Transformed Path Query
transformed_path_query.description: Internal field to track if path-based query was transformed. Not exposed to API.

transformed_kql_operator.title: Transformed Kql Operator
transformed_kql_operator.description: Internal field to track if a KQL operator was transformed. Not exposed to API.

transformed_parent_query.title: Transformed Parent Query
transformed_parent_query.description: Internal field to track if parent: filter was stripped from query. Not exposed to API.

transformed_wildcard_query.title: Transformed Wildcard Query
transformed_wildcard_query.description: Internal field to track if wildcard characters were removed from query. Not exposed to API.

tools.name: Search SharePoint Sites
tools.description: Search SharePoint sites visible to an organizational Microsoft account.

query.title: Query
query.description: Free-text keywords to match across SharePoint site properties. Required for the first page; omit when page_token is provided.

order_by.title: Order By
order_by.description: Optional creation-time ordering. This endpoint supports only createdDateTime asc or createdDateTime desc.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: Maximum sites to request on the first page. Must be between 1 and 999; Microsoft Graph may return fewer.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit it initially, then pass next_page_token back unchanged. The token carries the original search, page size, and ordering.

tools.name: Delete Drive Following
tools.description: Tool to unfollow a driveItem by removing it from the user's followed items collection. Use when you need to stop following a file or folder that was previously marked to follow.

id.title: Id
id.description: The unique identifier of the driveItem to unfollow. This is the ID of an item in the user's followed items collection.

tools.name: Update Drive Item Metadata
tools.description: Tool to update the metadata of a specific item (file or folder) in OneDrive. Use this to rename items, change descriptions, or move items to a new parent folder.

name.title: Name
name.description: The new name for the drive item. Must not contain illegal characters: `\`, `/`, `:`, `*`, `?`, `'`, `<`, `>`, `|`; these trigger an `invalidRequest` error.
name.human_parameter_description: What you want to rename the file or folder to. Enter the full new name, including the extension for files.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item (file or folder) to update.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the file or folder you want to update. You can copy this from a previous search/list result or from the item’s URL in OneDrive.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of the site. Used when updating an item within a site's drive.
site_id.human_parameter_description: If the item is stored in a SharePoint site’s drive, enter that site’s ID. Use this when targeting a site instead of a user, group, or specific drive.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user. Used when updating an item within a specific user's drive.
user_id.human_parameter_description: If the item belongs to a specific user’s OneDrive, enter that user’s ID (or use 'me' for your own). Use this instead of Group ID, Site ID, or Drive ID.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. Required if not using other specific paths like /me, /groups/{group-id}, /sites/{site-id}, or /users/{user-id}.
drive_id.human_parameter_description: Provide this if the item is in a specific drive you want to target. Leave it blank if you’re using your own drive or selecting a group, site, or user instead.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of the group. Used when updating an item within a group's drive.
group_id.human_parameter_description: If the file or folder is in a Microsoft 365 group’s drive, enter that group’s ID. Use this instead of Drive ID, Site ID, or User ID.

if_match.title: If Match
if_match.description: The eTag or cTag value for conditional update. If this header is included and the eTag provided doesn't match the current eTag on the item, a 412 Precondition Failed response is returned. Use this to prevent conflicts when multiple users update the same item.
if_match.human_parameter_description: Provide the current eTag of the item to ensure you're updating the latest version. This prevents accidental overwrites when multiple people are editing. Leave blank to skip this check.

description.title: Description
description.description: The new description for the drive item.
description.human_parameter_description: A short summary or notes about the item to help others understand it. Leave blank to keep the current description.

file_system_info.title: FileSystemInfo

createdDateTime.title: Created Date Time
createdDateTime.description: The UTC date and time the file was created on a client. ISO 8601 format.

lastAccessedDateTime.title: Last Accessed Date Time
lastAccessedDateTime.description: The UTC date and time the file was last accessed. ISO 8601 format.

lastModifiedDateTime.title: Last Modified Date Time
lastModifiedDateTime.description: The UTC date and time the file was last modified on a client. ISO 8601 format.

file_system_info.human_parameter_description: Set client-side file system timestamps. Useful for preserving original file creation and modification dates when syncing files from a local device.

parent_reference_id.title: Parent Reference Id
parent_reference_id.description: The ID of the new parent item. Use this to move the item. The driveId of the parentReference can also be specified if moving between drives. For cross-drive moves, `parent_reference_drive_id` is required alongside this field. Omit both fields when only renaming or updating metadata to avoid unintended moves.
parent_reference_id.human_parameter_description: The destination folder’s item ID if you want to move this file or folder. Combine with Parent Drive ID if moving to a different drive.

parent_reference_drive_id.title: Parent Reference Drive Id
parent_reference_drive_id.description: The drive ID of the new parent item, if moving to a different drive.
parent_reference_drive_id.human_parameter_description: Only needed if you’re moving the item to a different drive. Enter the ID of the drive where the destination folder lives.

tools.name: Update Drive Item Permissions
tools.description: Tool to update the roles of an existing permission on a OneDrive drive item. Use when you need to change the access level (read, write, owner) for a specific permission on a file or folder.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Array of Microsoft Graph role strings to assign to the permission. Documented/common values include read, write, and owner for SharePoint/OneDrive for Business permission resources; tenant/resource-specific roles may also be accepted by Graph.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive item.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The unique identifier of a SharePoint site. Use this if the item is in a SharePoint site's drive.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The unique identifier of a user. Use this if the item is in a specific user's drive (other than 'me').

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive. Required if not using other identifiers like group_id, site_id, or user_id.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: The unique identifier of a group. Use this if the item is in a group's drive.

permission_id.title: Permission Id
permission_id.description: The unique identifier of the permission to update.

tools.name: Update SharePoint Item Permission
tools.description: Update an application permission on a SharePoint list or list item using Microsoft Graph beta.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Roles to set on the permission, such as read or write.
roles.human_parameter_description: The access level to set, for example read or write.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: Optional SharePoint list item ID. Provide this to update a list-item permission; omit it to update a list-level permission.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The list item ID when updating list-item permission. Leave empty for list-level permissions.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The unique Microsoft Graph ID of the SharePoint list.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The Microsoft Graph SharePoint site ID in composite format, usually 'hostname,site-collection-id,web-id'.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The SharePoint site ID containing the list or list item.

permission_id.title: Permission Id
permission_id.description: The Microsoft Graph permission ID to update.
permission_id.human_parameter_description: The permission ID returned by the corresponding permission listing endpoint.

tools.name: Update SharePoint List Item Fields
tools.description: Update field values on a SharePoint list item using Microsoft Graph through the OneDrive connection. Use when you need to modify one or more columns on an existing SharePoint list item.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Field values to update, keyed by SharePoint internal column name. Only supplied fields are changed; all other list item fields are left as-is.
fields.human_parameter_description: The column values to update. Use SharePoint internal column names such as Status or Title.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The unique ID of the SharePoint list item to update.
item_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of the SharePoint list item to update.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: The unique Microsoft Graph ID of the SharePoint list that contains the item. Use ONE_DRIVE_LIST_SITE_LISTS to find list IDs.
list_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID of the SharePoint list that contains the item.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: The Microsoft Graph SharePoint site ID in composite format, usually 'hostname,site-collection-id,web-id'.
site_id.human_parameter_description: The SharePoint site ID that contains the list item. It usually looks like hostname,GUID,GUID.

if_match.title: If Match
if_match.description: Optional eTag for optimistic concurrency. If provided and it does not match the current list item eTag, Microsoft Graph returns 412 Precondition Failed.
if_match.human_parameter_description: Optional eTag to prevent overwriting someone else's change.

tools.name: Update Table Column Range
tools.description: Update values, formulas, number formats, or row and column visibility in a table column's whole or data-body range.

values.title: Values
values.description: Two-dimensional array of raw values to write.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: DriveItem ID of the Office Open XML workbook.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: Drive containing the workbook. Use 'me' for the connected user's drive, or provide a Microsoft Graph drive ID.

formulas.title: Formulas
formulas.description: Two-dimensional array of A1-style formulas or literal values to write.

range_kind.title: Range Kind
range_kind.description: Use data_body for data rows only, or whole_column to include the table column's header and totals ranges.

row_hidden.title: Row Hidden
row_hidden.description: Whether all rows in the range should be hidden.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Optional workbook session ID returned by ONE_DRIVE_CREATE_WORKBOOK_SESSION.

column_index.title: Column Index
column_index.description: Zero-based index of the table column to update.

column_hidden.title: Column Hidden
column_hidden.description: Whether all columns in the range should be hidden.

formulas_r1c1.title: Formulas R1C1
formulas_r1c1.description: Two-dimensional array of R1C1-style formulas or literal values to write.

number_format.title: Number Format
number_format.description: Two-dimensional array of Excel number format strings to write.

formulas_local.title: Formulas Local
formulas_local.description: Two-dimensional array of A1-style formulas or literal values in the user's language and number-formatting locale.

table_id_or_name.title: Table Id Or Name
table_id_or_name.description: Exact table ID or table name in the workbook.

tools.name: Write Workbook Cell
tools.description: Updates the value, formula, or format of a specific cell in an Excel workbook stored in OneDrive. Use this action when you need to write data to a single cell at a specific row and column position. The row and column parameters are 0-indexed (row 0 is the first row, column 0 is column A).

row.title: Row
row.description: The row number of the cell (0-indexed). Row 0 is the first row in the worksheet.

column.title: Column
column.description: The column number of the cell (0-indexed). Column 0 is the first column (A) in the worksheet.

values.title: Values
values.description: Optional 2D array containing the value to write to the cell. Must be a single-cell array like [['new value']]. At least one of values, formulas, or number_format must be provided.

item_id.title: Item Id
item_id.description: The ID of the workbook item (Excel file) in OneDrive.

drive_id.title: Drive Id
drive_id.description: The ID of the drive containing the workbook. Use 'me' for the user's default OneDrive, or specify a SharePoint drive ID.

formulas.title: Formulas
formulas.description: Optional 2D array containing a formula to set in the cell (e.g., [['=SUM(A1:A10)']]). If provided, this takes precedence over values.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Optional workbook session ID. If provided, changes are grouped in a session for better consistency. Must be a valid session ID from a createSession call.

number_format.title: Number Format
number_format.description: Optional 2D array containing the number format string for the cell (e.g., [['0.00']] for two decimal places, [['mm-dd-yyyy']] for dates).

worksheet_id_or_name.title: Worksheet Id Or Name
worksheet_id_or_name.description: The ID or name of the worksheet where the cell is located. Can be the worksheet name (e.g., 'Sheet1') or its unique ID.
